contract.intent: AUTO ACCEPT MUST ACTUALLY FIRE. Measured 2026-09-26: the review worker was run against the configured provider on a CLONE, twice, on deliveries the floor had already certified closeable (every AC claimed, every claim's check captured and passing) — and BOTH returned `human`. Zero accepts. So D-1, the operator premise that the human leaves the exit gate, is currently INERT: it removes no burden, and the auto review alone makes every gate more to read, not less. THE CAUSE IS NOT THE VERDICT RULE. Applying the obvious rule change (let `quality` stop blocking) to the findings both runs actually landed yields `human` and `human` — identical to the current rule. Both runs are blocked by `uncertain`, and the rule is right to block: it refuses to auto-accept a criterion it could not verify, and one of those `uncertain`s (run 2 F7, `transferNotLive` returning undefined on a failed read, and whether `gate!` refuses it by name first) is a REAL finding. Tuning the middle row to reach an accept here would be tuning it to swallow a real one. THE CAUSE IS THE MATERIAL. Two named gaps, and the first is a pure omission: (1) `buildReviewMaterial` reads `brief(full)`, which ALREADY exposes `conclusion.claims` — each claim's AC, the author's statement, the mapped `check`, and that check RESOLVED with its result, source, detail and sha — and the material carries the `checks` list but NOT the claims. So the reviewer reads an UNORDERED list of runs and cannot tell which one the author stands behind for which criterion; on the measured task four distinct criteria all mapped to one `npm test` pass and the material never said so. (2) The material carries no test content at all: `grep -c 'test('` over the assembled 80,267-char prompt returns 0, and test files appear only as stat lines in the change map. So the link 'this suite pass covers AC-3' is author-typed prose that nothing on the record or in the material can confirm — and the reviewer can see it is unconfirmed. Its every `uncertain` has ONE shape, and it is a request for criterion-level evidence: 'I would need either the gate! transfer-branch code or an e2e case for an unknown id to settle it' · 'I would need a browser-level check (the tests are jsdom-style)'. THIS NODE CARRIES THAT EVIDENCE. IT IS NOT A PROMPT REWRITE and not a rule change: the same findings shape, the same severity vocabulary, the same deterministic rule, the same ONE gate writer, and the model still never asked for a verdict. WHAT IS EXPLICITLY OUT OF SCOPE: the agentic read/edit/run loop (the shell and tool abilities are UNBUILT by design and the reviewer needs none of them — every piece it asked for is derivable from the record and git, deterministically, before the call); and any change to the three arms' semantics.
acceptanceCriteria: AC-1 — THE CLAIMS ARE CARRIED, AND THE REVIEWER CAN SEE WHAT THE AUTHOR STANDS BEHIND. `buildReviewMaterial` states, per criterion, the author's claim as the record holds it: the AC (id and its VERBATIM contract text), the claim's statement, the mapped `check`, and that mapping RESOLVED against the log — the bound run's result, source (captured vs reported), sha and detail — or an explicit statement that the mapping is UNBOUND, which is a finding rather than prose. Nothing is typed by the assembly: every field comes from `brief`. Pinned by test: a fixture with claims whose checks differ renders each claim beside ITS check, a fixture with an unbound claim says so rather than omitting it, and an unclaimed AC is NAMED as unclaimed.

AC-2 — THE CRITERION-LEVEL EVIDENCE IS CARRIED. For each claim, the material also carries the TEST CONTENT behind it, so the reviewer can judge whether the mapped run's assertions actually cover the criterion — the question it kept asking and could not answer. The selection is DETERMINISTIC and derived (the claim's own statement and evidence pointers · the test files the reviewed range touches · the mapped check's command), never hand-authored, and it is BOUNDED with its bound stated the way the existing cut states its own. Pinned by test: the tests a claim names appear in the material, and a long selection is cut with its length named rather than silently truncated.

AC-3 — THE ACCEPT ARM FIRES, DEMONSTRATED AND NOT ASSERTED. The worker, run against the configured provider on a delivery whose criteria are text-decidable, returns `accept`, and the accept CLOSES the task through the existing writer with `decider: worker` — the whole point of the node. The demonstration is reproducible: the amendment names the delivery, the run, the findings and the verdict, and the harness that produced it stays usable. A run that still returns `human` is NOT a pass, and the node reports the actual verdict rather than a hoped-for one.

AC-4 — WHAT CANNOT BE CARRIED IS STATED, NOT SILENT. The material NAMES its own limits — what falls outside the selection and why — so an `uncertain` raised against a known limit is a stated boundary rather than a surprise, and a reviewer that raises one can be seen to be asking for something the material already declared absent. Some criteria need evidence no text carries (run 2's F8 wanted a real browser because the tests are jsdom-style); the material must say so where it applies rather than leaving the reviewer to discover it. Pinned by test.

AC-5 — NO REGRESSION. The three arms keep their semantics and stay pinned: open gap/regression → rework · open uncertain with no defect → the human with NO rejection burned · all matches/resolved → accept. `npm test` green, `npm run typecheck` and `npm run build` clean, the captured checks recorded via capture!, `ann check` + `ann verify` clean, committed with structured evidence (F-AC18). The claims carried in the material are the SAME facts the card and the floor read, so the worker and the human still cannot read different records (12/22 AC-6).
expectedOutputs: the claims carried into `buildReviewMaterial`'s assembly, each beside the check the record resolves for it (src/flow)
the criterion-level test content carried per claim, selected deterministically and bounded with its bound stated (src/flow)
the material's own limits NAMED where they apply, so a known boundary is distinguishable from an unseen one (src/flow)
tests: claims rendered against their own checks · an unbound claim named · an unclaimed AC named · the named tests present · the bound stated when cut · the three arms unchanged
the live demonstration: the worker against the configured provider returns accept on a text-decidable delivery and the task closes with decider: worker, recorded with its evidence
